label: hv-morph-turing
topic: Reaction-diffusion (Turing) pattern statements: onset wavelength, activator/inhibitor diffusivity, stripe insertion with growth, digit number vs. wavelength and domain size
summary:
Harvested 11 statements; 2 validated against fetched numbers (both pass); the Lean file was written but NOT checked (both allowed check runs failed on a missing Mathlib build file, an environment error, not a reported proof error), so nothing here counts as proved.

Registry status: `turing-ddi` and `turing-wavelength` (both v1.1.0, status candidate) already cover the instability condition and the onset wavenumber on an unbounded domain. `turing-wavelength` explicitly lists finite-domain mode quantisation as NOT established; that gap is what the new statements (S8-S10) and the unchecked Lean file target. Grep of lean/ and tracks/lean showed no other law ids on this topic; tracks/research has hits in phase2/verify-t2-patterns-*.json which I did not open.

Validations (article details according to PubMed; numbers read from the PMC full texts):
- V1 PASS. Prediction (turing-ddi: inhibitor must diffuse faster than activator). Measured in zebrafish embryo (Muller 2012, https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1221920): Cyclops 0.7 +/- 0.2, Squint 3.2 +/- 0.5 (activators); Lefty1 11.1 +/- 0.6, Lefty2 18.9 +/- 3.0 um^2/s (inhibitors). All four inhibitor/activator ratios exceed 1 (3.5, 5.9, 15.9, 27.0, my arithmetic). Caveat: this tests only the necessary inequality, not the full Turing inequality, which needs the kinetic Jacobian.
- V2 PASS (ordinal only). Prediction (S9: at fixed handplate width, shorter wavelength gives at least as many digits, so digit count is non-decreasing as distal Hox dose falls). Measured (Sheth 2012, https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1226804): 7-9, then 8-9, then 9-11, then at least 12-14 digits; authors state the increase did not rely on larger handplate size. Monotone, as predicted. Caveat: digit period values are only in figures (1C, 4B, 4C), so the quantitative form (period x count = width) is untested; the Hoxa13-null class (7-8 condensations, count "could not be precisely determined") was left out of the ordering.

Not verified today: Turing 1952 itself (cited via the registry files only), the marine angelfish stripe-insertion paper and the Kondo-Miura 2010 review (my PMIDs for both were wrong and returned unrelated papers), and any measured stripe spacing in zebrafish. S4, S6, S7, S10, S11 are untested.

Files: D:/Users/ashenoy00000/delphi-work/agents4/hv-morph-turing/TuringFiniteDomain.lean (unchecked). The folder also has src/PMC3525670.xml and src/PMC4486416.xml, two 150-byte failed downloads that can be deleted.

findings.claim: S1 Diffusion-driven instability. Formal: for u_t=f+Du*lap u, v_t=g+Dv*lap v with fu+gv<0, det J>0, a spatial mode is unstable iff Dv*fu+Du*gv > 2*sqrt(Du*Dv*det J); this forces Du != Dv. Assumptions: two species, linearisation, fixed domain. ALREADY IN REGISTRY as turing-ddi v1.1.0 (candidate). Falsifying test: measured D of an identified activator/inhibitor pair with inhibitor not faster (see S3).
findings.evidence_quote: the two diffusivities are necessarily unequal
findings.confidence: high for registry status; primary paper not opened in this run

findings.claim: S2 Onset wavelength. Formal: k_c^2 = sqrt(det J/(Du*Dv)), lambda_c = 2*pi/k_c; scaling both D by m multiplies lambda_c by sqrt(m); tissue size does not appear. Assumptions: onset, unbounded domain. ALREADY IN REGISTRY as turing-wavelength v1.1.0 (candidate, constraint TURINGLAMBDA1). Falsifying test: pattern spacing vs. measured sqrt(D) across perturbations in a system with measured D and kinetics; no single open dataset with all inputs found.
findings.evidence_quote: the critical wavelength grows as the square root of the diffusivity scale

findings.claim: S3 (VALIDATED, PASS) In the zebrafish Nodal/Lefty activator/inhibitor pair the inhibitor has the higher effective diffusion coefficient. Formal: D_Lefty > D_Nodal. Not in registry as a data row (turing-ddi has empty observations). Dataset: FRAP values in Muller et al. 2012 (PMC3525670). Test: any inhibitor/activator ratio <= 1 within error falsifies. Result: ratios 3.5 to 27, all > 1.
findings.evidence_quote: 11.1 ± 0.6 μm2/s for Lefty1-GFP, and 18.9 ± 3.0 μm2/s for Lefty2-GFP
findings.confidence: high (numbers read from full text via fetch tool; ratios are my arithmetic)

findings.claim: S4 Signalling range follows diffusivity when clearance is similar. Formal: gradient length = sqrt(D/k); with equal k, range_Lefty/range_Nodal = sqrt(D_L/D_N), e.g. sqrt(18.9/3.2) = 2.43 for Lefty2 vs Squint. Assumption: steady-state exponential gradient, uniform clearance. Not in registry. Dataset: gradient profiles and half-lives in the same paper's supplement. Test: measured range ratio outside the predicted ratio's error band. UNTESTED: I did not fetch the measured ranges or half-lives.
findings.evidence_quote: Nodals and Leftys have similar clearance kinetics
findings.confidence: medium; prediction computed, measurement not fetched

findings.claim: S5 (VALIDATED, PASS, ordinal) Digit number rises as distal Hox dose falls in the Gli3-null mouse limb, without a larger handplate: read as Hox dose setting the Turing wavelength. Formal: N(dose) non-increasing in dose at fixed width L; with N = floor(L/lambda), lambda falls with dose. Not in registry (the Sheth DOI is only a see_also of turing-wavelength). Dataset: genotype digit counts and Fig 1C digit periods in Sheth et al. 2012. Test: a lower-dose genotype with fewer digits at equal width falsifies. Result: 7-9 -> 8-9 -> 9-11 -> at least 12-14, monotone.
findings.evidence_quote: to at least 12 to 14 digits when only one copy of Hoxa13 remained
findings.confidence: medium-high; counts read from text; wavelength values are in figures only and were not extracted; Hoxa13-null class excluded (count not precisely determinable)

findings.claim: S6 Digit patterning is driven by a three-component Bmp-Sox9-Wnt Turing network modulated by morphogen gradients. Formal: periodic Sox9(x) along the anterior-posterior axis with period set by network parameters; gradients modulate wavelength along the proximo-distal axis. Not in registry (DOI is a see_also only). Dataset: Sox9 limb-bud expression images from the paper / eMouseAtlas (not opened). Test: Bmp or Wnt inhibition failing to change Sox9 stripe period in the predicted direction. UNTESTED.
findings.evidence_quote: a Turing network implemented by Bmp, Sox9, and Wnt drives digit specification
findings.confidence: medium; abstract only, no numbers extracted

findings.claim: S7 Zebrafish stripe cells satisfy the Turing sign structure: short-range mutual exclusion of melanophores and xanthophores, long-range support of melanophores by xanthophores. Formal: interaction kernel w(r) < 0 for r < r1 and > 0 for r1 < r < r2 (local inhibition, lateral activation of the other type), equivalent to short-range activation with long-range inhibition. Not in registry. Dataset: laser-ablation outcomes in Nakamasu et al. 2009 (PMC2689028, not opened in full). Test: ablating distant xanthophores not reducing melanophore survival falsifies. UNTESTED; no stripe spacing number obtained.
findings.evidence_quote: the local effect of these cells is opposite to that of their effects long range

findings.claim: S8 Stripe insertion with growth: new palate ridges (Shh stripes) appear where the gap between existing ridges has widened; FGF and Shh act as activator and inhibitor. Formal: at fixed lambda, stripe count n with n*lambda <= L < (n+1)*lambda is non-decreasing in L (theorem count_mono_in_size in my Lean file, UNCHECKED). Not in registry (finite-domain behaviour is listed as not established). Dataset: ruga-spacing time series in Economou et al. 2012 (PMC3303118, not opened in full). Test: gap at insertion not near twice the baseline spacing, or count decreasing with growth.
findings.evidence_quote: appear at two growth zones where the space between previously laid rugae increases
findings.confidence: medium; abstract only; Lean statement not machine-checked

findings.claim: S9 Fixed domain, shorter wavelength, at least as many repeats. Formal: if n*lam <= L < (m+1)*lam' with 0 < lam and lam' <= lam then n <= m (theorem count_mono_in_wavelength, UNCHECKED). This is the arithmetic behind S5. Not in registry. Dataset and test: as S5, plus the quantitative version period x count = handplate width using Fig 1C values.
findings.evidence_quote: the dose of distal Hox genes modulates the digit period or wavelength
findings.confidence: low as a proved result (file failed to check); the mathematics is elementary

findings.claim: S10 Minimum domain size. Formal: with no-flux boundaries the admissible wavenumbers are n*pi/L; if the unstable band ends at k_hi and L*k_hi < pi, no mode n >= 1 is unstable, so no pattern forms below L_min = pi/k_hi (theorem no_mode_below_critical_size, UNCHECKED). Standard textbook consequence of S1; I did not open a primary source for it. Not in registry. Dataset: none identified; a test needs pattern onset size in a growing tissue plus an independent wavelength estimate. UNTESTED.
findings.confidence: low: no primary source opened, Lean file not checked

findings.claim: S11 Inhibitor dose sets spacing in mouse skin: overexpressing the inhibitor DKK lowers hair follicle density, and moderate WNT suppression clusters follicles. Formal: follicle density is non-increasing in inhibitor production rate. Not in registry. Dataset: follicle density counts in Sick et al. 2006 (full text not opened). Test: DKK overexpression line with unchanged or higher follicle density. UNTESTED.
findings.evidence_quote: Transgenic DKK overexpression reduces overall appendage density

key_claims: Registry already holds turing-ddi and turing-wavelength (both candidate); finite-domain mode quantisation is explicitly not covered and is the gap worth filling.
V1 pass: measured inhibitor (Lefty) diffusion coefficients exceed activator (Nodal) ones by 3.5x to 27x, as the instability condition requires.
V2 pass (ordinal): digit count rises monotonically 7-9, 8-9, 9-11, >=12-14 as distal Hox dose falls with no larger handplate.
The Lean file TuringFiniteDomain.lean did NOT check: both runs failed reading a Mathlib .olean.private file (a different file each run), so no theorem in it is proved.

lay_summary: Some animal patterns, like stripes and the row of fingers, may form because two chemicals spread through tissue at different speeds: one switches things on nearby, the other switches things off farther away.
The maths says the 'off' chemical must spread faster, and a zebrafish experiment we looked up found exactly that: it spreads about 3 to 27 times faster.

The maths also says that if the repeat distance gets shorter while the space stays the same, more repeats fit; mice with fewer copies of certain genes grew more and thinner digits, from about 8 up to 12-14, which matches.
We wrote a computer-checked proof of the 'more repeats fit' idea, but the proof checker on this machine was broken, so it has not been confirmed yet.
Several other statements were collected but not yet tested against numbers.

glossary.reaction-diffusion (Turing) system: Two or more chemicals that react with each other and spread through tissue, which can make repeating patterns by themselves.
glossary.activator: A chemical that increases its own production and that of the inhibitor nearby.
glossary.inhibitor: A chemical that shuts the activator down and spreads farther.
glossary.diffusion coefficient (D): How fast a substance spreads, in square micrometres per second.
glossary.wavelength / period: The distance from one stripe or digit to the next.
glossary.wavenumber (k): 2*pi divided by the wavelength; a bigger k means tighter stripes.
glossary.Jacobian (J), det J: The table of how each chemical's rate changes with each chemical's amount; det J is one number computed from it.
glossary.onset: The point where the even, pattern-free state just becomes unstable.
glossary.no-flux boundary: An edge that chemicals cannot cross.
glossary.mode: One allowed wave shape that fits in the tissue.
glossary.Nodal, Lefty: A signalling protein (activator) and its blocker (inhibitor) in early fish embryos; Cyclops and Squint are two Nodal proteins.
glossary.Hox genes, Gli3: Genes that control body and limb layout; removing them here changes digit number.
glossary.handplate: The flat paddle at the end of an embryonic limb where digits form.
glossary.Sox9, Bmp, Wnt, Shh, FGF, DKK: Signalling molecules or markers used by cells in developing tissue; DKK blocks Wnt.
glossary.melanophore, xanthophore: Black and yellow pigment cells in fish skin.
glossary.rugae: Ridges on the roof of the mouth.
glossary.FRAP: A microscope method that bleaches a glowing spot and times how fast glow returns, to measure spreading speed.
glossary.clearance: How quickly a molecule is removed.
glossary.Lean / Mathlib: A program that checks mathematical proofs, and its library of known mathematics.
glossary.named hypothesis: An assumption written out explicitly in a proof instead of being hidden.
glossary.ordinal test: A test of order only (more or fewer), not of exact amounts.
